newsitem.title: USA: White House says Shalikashvili plans to step down.
newsitem.headline: White House says Shalikashvili plans to step down.

text.p: The White House said on Wednesday Gen. John Shalikashvili, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS), has told Secretary of Defence William Cohen he intends to step down in September.

The 60-year-old Army general, who was born in Warsaw, Poland, has served two two-year terms as the nation's top military officer under Clinton. His decision to step down would be in keeping with the tradition for JCS chairmen, none of whom has served more than two terms.
"He has indicated to the secretary of defence that he plans to retire at the end of the fiscal year," White House spokesman David Johnson told reporters. The current fiscal year ends on Sept. 30.
Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters on Tuesday Shalikashvili wanted to retire after more than 37 years in the military and would not accept an appointment to a third term.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said the president had not decided who might replace Shalikashvili and Gen. George Joulwan, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander, Europe, who has said he plans to retire in the spring after 36 years of service.
"Obviously the president will be looking for the strongest candidate who will continue the excellent service that we have enjoyed in those posts," McCurry added.
